newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo corn futures end higher on weak yen.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo corn futures end higher on weak yen.

text.p: Tokyo corn futures closed higher across the board on Thursday, supported by the yen's steep fall against the dollar, traders said.
Prices were 170 to 300 yen higher, with the benchmark May 1998 contract closing 170 yen up at 14,330 yen per tonne.
The day's estimated trading volume was 29,047 lots.

The dollar climbed above 115 yen, compared with the Wednesday U.S. level of 111.29, due to a comment by a senior Finance Ministry official that Japan's trade surplus will not be a major issue at the Group of Seven nations' meeting in Denver.
"Today's factor was the weak yen. That's all," a brokerage house trader said.
The spot July corn contract on the CBOT Project A overnight trading system stood at $2.72-3/4 per bushel at 0815 GMT, against $2.72-1/2 at Wednesday's close.
Spot July CBOT soybean futures were trading at $8.30-3/4 a bushel at 0815 GMT, up from $8.30-1/2 at Wednesday's close.
